subject: Fwd: AtlasEdge renewal - term uplift and capacity acceleration (approval requested)
messages:
From: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@atlasedge.com>

Cc: Priya Naik <priya.naik@atlasedge.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T14:02:00Z
Subject: AtlasEdge: Upcoming renewal — need to scale Dedicated pool + SLA

Ben —

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for the dedicated pool is coming up in late July and our usage has grown faster than expected. We want to move from our current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 40-GPU pool (steady-state), with a 6–8 week ramp. Key asks from our side:

- Firm throughput SLO (p95 < 250ms for inference at 512 tokens) for the committed pool
- Pricing for 12- and 24-month terms with committed capacity pricing
- Any promotional credits or ramp credits you can extend given the size of the uplift

Attached a quick usage export for Q1 to give you context. We’re budgeting but need a firm proposal by next week to validate with procurement.

Can you propose options and any standard ramp/credit structures you’d offer for this type of uplift?

Thanks,
Sam Hayes
Head of Platform Engineering
AtlasEdge

Attachment: AtlasEdge_Usage_Q1.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-18T18:11:00Z
Subject: Re: AtlasEdge: Upcoming renewal — need to scale Dedicated pool + SLA

Sam —

Appreciate the heads up and the usage file. Congrats on the growth — reasonable ask. High level options we can move quickly on:

1) 40-GPU committed pool, 12-month term — list price + promotional ramp credit equal to 20% of month-1 bill (applied first 3 months) + standard support.
2) 40-GPU committed pool, 24-month term — 15% recurring discount + 3-month ramp credit (equivalent to 25% month-1) + throughput SLO add-on.
3) 48-GPU option for peak bursts (auto-burst), billed on usage with a small committed base — for customers who need headroom.

I’ve attached a preliminary price worksheet (Proposed_MA_Pricing.pdf). To firm anything up I’ll need procurement numbers and a target discount/credit they expect.

If you’re available I can schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to run through the options and get procurement language together.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Proposed_MA_Pricing.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Internal: AtlasEdge renewal — request 40-GPU pool + 3mo ramp credit (DEAL-2027-ATLE-042)

Laura/Markus/Marissa —

Summary: AtlasEdge is asking to move from 16 -> 40 GPUs at renewal (target effective date: 2027-07-25). Procurement has requested a one-time commercial credit of ~$50k and a p95 throughput SLA with service-credit remedy. They’ve asked for final pricing next week.

Proposal I’d like to present:
- 12-month committed term
- 40-GPU reserved pool (steady-state), 6–8 week ramp
- 15% recurring discount on list pricing for year 1
- Ramp package: 3 months of ramp credits: 20% month-1, 10% month-2, 5% month-3 (equates to roughly $48k based on expected billing)
- SLA: p95 latency < 250ms; service credits up to 5% invoice for breach (subject to legal review)

Why: Upsell is strategic (platform dependency, increasing usage). Proposal is aggressive but keeps gross margin within acceptable bounds.

Ask: Can Finance/Legal sign off on the ramp-credit construct and the ~$48–50k commercial concession? If not, what ceiling should I present to the customer so we can close on timeline?

Attachments: Proposed_MA_Pricing.pdf, Committed_Pool_SLA_Draft.pdf

Thanks,
Ben

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-21T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: AtlasEdge renewal — request 40-GPU pool + 3mo ramp credit (DEAL-2027-ATLE-042)

Ben/Team —

I reviewed the numbers. The business case for the expansion looks solid, but the $48–50k upfront concession is outside standard approval for Sales Ops. Finance can approve up to $30k in commercial concessions for renewal upsells without exec sign-off, but anything above $30k requires approval from VP Sales (rishi_malhotra) and CFO.

Recommendation: Present a $30k immediate commercial credit with a structured milestone for incremental credits tied to usage ramp (e.g., $10k after reaching 70% steady-state for 2 consecutive months). This preserves payroll and aligns incentives.

If Sales wants to proceed with the full ~$50k up-front, escalate to Rishi for exec sign-off.

-Markus
Head of Finance
Redwood Inference

Procurement is requesting a one-time commercial credit of ~$50k to offset ramping costs. I’ve proposed a 3-month ramp credit (20% / 10% / 5%) which amounts to roughly $48k.
